current.text: He is a projected starter for Washington. He plays center on offense, and Alex Sarr moves to power forward.
He is projected for about 32 minutes per game.
He and Trae Young are expected to take most of Washington's offensive usage, ahead of AJ Dybantsa and Alex Sarr.
There have been trade rumors involving Golden State.
Experts expect Washington to keep him and push for the playoffs, but a trade cannot be ruled out. The team could reconsider around the trade deadline.
Washington is trying to compete for the play-in, so the late-season rest and minutes cuts of past years should not happen.
Washington has only 14 back-to-backs this season and one in the fantasy playoffs. Experts see this as good for him.
He played only 20 games last season.
His draft position keeps sliding. Experts call the slide an overreaction.
Experts see him as good value in round 3, around picks 24 to 30. At his Yahoo rank of about 44 he is an easy pick and a sleeper.
His ESPN rank of 14 is too high to draft him there.
Per game he could rank about 14th and has top 10 upside. Experts drop him 6 to 7 spots in their rankings for injury risk.
If he plays 60 to 62 games, a mid-20s pick is a very good one.
Paired with Victor Wembanyama he makes blocks and rebounds strong, but the team then needs guard stats.

durable.text: His blocks and rebounds are league outliers. He also helps FG% and points.
His outside shooting and perimeter game decline every year. He rarely shoots anything except at the rim.
He is now a worse rim protector than Alex Sarr.
He has a long history of lower-body injuries of several different kinds. In Dallas he never played five games in a row before getting hurt.
He is 33 but can still be productive when on the floor.
He is better in category leagues than in points leagues.
Because he misses games often, he is worth a bit more in roto than in head-to-head.

note: Davis gives elite blocks and rebounds plus help in FG% and points. He has no category flagged as weak, so he fits any build that can live with his missed games (projected 58 to 61 games). The experts' round 3 range lines up with his Yahoo average cost of 21.8 USD and ESPN average cost of 24.4 USD, so he is a buy in the low to mid 20s USD. ESPN's 46 USD value and our league's 54 USD from last season assume a healthy season. Early on, check his games played and minutes (about 32 projected), and watch for trade news before the 2027-03-04 deadline.
